newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower as soy, wheat falter.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower as soy, wheat falter.

text.p: CBOT soy products ended lower on Friday, pressured by a late sell-off in wheat and bearish news out of the soybean pit, traders said.
Wheat futures dropped late on renewed talk India and Egypt would bypass U.S. wheat supplies in their upcoming wheat purchases, traders said.
Soybeans struggled all session on news benefical rains fell in Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul soybean growing regions.
Soyoil fell sharply on the open as Dean Witter and Merrill Lynch sold the March but commercial buying underpinned the market, traders said.

They said Dean Witter sold 200 lots March early and Merrill Lynch sold at least 500 lots. Funds sold at least 2,200 lots on the day. Griffin Trading sold 1,000 lots March while Smith Barney and Prudential Securities each sold 300.
But ADM bought 500 March, Cargill Inc bought 600 March, 300 May and 200 July. Produce Grain and Term Commodities were also buyers on the day.
ADM and Continental Grain each bought 300 March soymeal while Produce Grain sold 500 March, 200 May and 200 July.
Soyoil ended down 0.12 to 0.05 per lb while soymeal ended down $1.20 to $0.60 per ton with March off $0.60 at $236.90.
Soyoil volume was estimated by CBOT at 15,000 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 16,913 lots. Soymeal volume was pegged at 20,000 lots, against Thursday's actual volume of 24,600.
